text:
## Delta review of edeba03 (after round 3)

**Verdict: needs maintainer.** 0 blocking, 2 should-fix, 4 notes. Nothing blocking remains in the code, and on the code alone this would be `review:approved`. The label is `review:needs-maintainer` for one reason that has nothing to do with `edeba03`: this pull request's diff against its base changes `CLAUDE.md`, and an agent bound by the rules cannot approve a change to them (see "The label" below).

Reviewed at `1561472`: `git diff f9d9ee3 edeba03` (the fix), `cf0cd39` (one test row after the merge of `b01-skeleton`), `1561472` (removal of a gitlink committed by mistake). The tree at the head holds nothing under `.claude/worktrees/` (`git ls-tree -r HEAD` has no such path). The implementer's replies were read as claims and every one I relied on was re-run.

### The label

`git diff --stat origin/b01-skeleton...HEAD -- CLAUDE.md .claude` is not empty: commit `5bac8bb` ("CLAUDE.md: the loop now commits, pushes and opens the pull request", from the first submission, the old `0e7f6a0`) is on this branch, and GitHub lists `CLAUDE.md` among the files of this pull request. The text it changes is the older seven-step loop, which `chore-agents` has since rewritten wholesale, so the content is superseded and harmless, but the rule is about who may approve, not about content. The maintainer can either accept it as is, or have the orchestrator take `CLAUDE.md` out of this diff (the file would then arrive through `chore-agents` alone).

### Status of the round 3 findings

| Round 3 finding | Status |
|---|---|
| blocking: connect failures put user, database, host and port into the error and the log | **resolved.** Re-run with markers on 15 failure paths of my own (list below), walking every wrapped error and printing each with `%v`, `%+v` and `%#v`, on top of the four paths the new tests drive: no marker anywhere |
| blocking: the empty-string case of the domain test could not fail (M1) | **resolved.** M1 is killed twice |
| should-fix (isolation): comments said `Bind` narrows a helper-role transaction | **resolved.** Comments, architecture 3.2 and 4, and the B10 backlog line say what Postgres does, a test pins it, and `Bind` refuses the transaction `RoleTx` hands out |
| should-fix: version check untested (M3) | **resolved.** M3 is killed by `TestCheckVersion` |
| should-fix: Go rule and SQL domain not tied together | **resolved.** 27 shared cases, two guards on the test itself |
| should-fix: goose lock polled every 5 s | **resolved.** Read `lock/session_locker_options.go` and `lock/postgres.go` of goose v3.28.0 in the module cache: `WithLockTimeout(period, failureThreshold)`, period in seconds, minimum 1 each, becomes `retry.WithMaxRetries(threshold, retry.NewConstant(period))`. 1 and 300 is one first attempt plus 300 retries one second apart, so the ceiling is five minutes plus the query time, as the comment and ADR 2 say. The locker is built per `Migrate` call, so the retry counter is not shared |
| should-fix: no connect timeout | **resolved**, with one edge left (inline, `connect_timeout=0`) |
| should-fix: dead code (`NewContext`, `FromContext`, `ErrNoTenant`, `DB.Ping`) | **resolved.** `git grep` on `origin/b04-outbox` and `origin/chore-agents`: only the definitions and their own tests, which those branches still carry because they have not merged this fix forward yet |
| should-fix: missing tests (migrate command, connect failures, panic and cancellation, Down) | **resolved**, except the wiring of `scrub` (inline, should-fix) |
| should-fix: Postgres 16 in the CI matrix | **not done, and said so.** Left for the maintainer to place. I agree it does not belong in this fix |
| should-fix: README status, PR description | description **resolved** (it matches the code; it says "as it is at `edeba03`" and the head is now three commits later, none of which changes behaviour). README deliberately left to `b04-outbox`, which rewrites it: accepted |

### Coverage, scaled to the delta

| Dimension | What I checked | Findings |
|---|---|---|
| Acceptance | the three Done-when lines of #3 are untouched by the delta; their tests still run and pass | 0 |
| Tests have teeth | the three round 3 survivors again, plus M4 to M10 below | 1 should-fix (M4 and M5 survive) |
| Tests are comprehensive | coverage of `store`, `tenancy`, `cmd`: `connError`, `scrub`, `describeSQLState`, `isTLSFailure`, `poolConfig`, `checkVersion`, `begin` at 100%; the error branch of `Migrate` and of `provider` never runs. Every new test has a deadline of its own; the blackhole test is bounded at 8 s and reports a leak before it may skip (an `Errorf` followed by `Skipf` is a failure in Go, confirmed under M6) | counted above |
| Correctness | order inside `connError` (server verdict, then context, then DNS, timeout, errno, TLS); `closeWithin`; the provider's close function on the error path; `cf0cd39` against `main.go` | 0 |
| Security: isolation, ordering, secrets | 15 failure paths with markers; what scrubbing leaves for callers to match; the `crossTenantTx` wrapper against savepoints, `pgx.BeginFunc`, batches, a second wrapper and `tx.Conn()`; import direction | 2 notes |
| Security: input, crypto, limits, dependencies | the only text taken from the far end of the connection and printed is the SQLSTATE, after a check for five characters of 0-9A-Z; a fake server that answers with HTTP and one that closes at once are both classified without echoing anything; no new dependency (`go mod tidy -diff` clean). `govulncheck` is not installed here, so it was not run | 0 |
| Performance | the lock period (store package 10 s here, was 21 s); connect timeout measured: 1.00 s with `connect_timeout=1`, 10.00 s by default | 0 |
| Dead code | callers of every identifier the delta adds or removes. `crossTenantTx.CrossTenant` has 0% coverage because it is a marker and is never called, which is its purpose | 0 |
| Codebase improvement | how `Bind` recognises the wrapper; what `scrub` does to an error that did not come from the pool | 2 notes (the same two) |
| Documentation | architecture 3.2 step 2 and section 4 against the code and against `origin/b04-outbox` (its `Claim` runs under `RoleTx` with a lease token and does no per-tenant work there, so the two-transaction text is true of where the code is going); ADR 2; backlog B10; godoc of `RoleTx`, `Bind`, `Open`, `Migrate`; the PR description | 1 should-fix (the same `connect_timeout=0` edge) |

Standing rules: `git log origin/b01-skeleton..origin/b03-store-rls --format='%h %(trailers:only,unfold)'` shows no trailer on any of the nine commits. No em dash in the delta or in the whole diff against the base, and none in the PR description.

**`make check`** at `1561472`: green (tidy, vet, golangci-lint 0 issues, `go test -race` with the integration tests running, not skipped). **CI** on the head: `check` passes.

### Mutations (each restored with `git checkout -- .`)

- **M1** domain `{1,64}` to `{0,64}` (survived in round 3): **killed** by `TestTenantIDDomainRejectsMalformedIDs` and `TestTheGoRuleAndTheDomainAgree/empty`.
- **M2** URL parse error wrapped with `%w` (survived in round 3): **killed** by `TestOpenNeverEchoesTheURL`.
- **M3** version check forced off (survived in round 3): **killed** by `TestCheckVersion`.
- **M4** `begin` returns `pgx.BeginFunc(...)` without `scrub`: **survived**, `./internal/store/` and `./cmd/...` green. Inline.
- **M5** both `scrub` calls removed from `Migrate`: **survived**, same run. Inline, same comment.
- **M6** the first `connError` in `preflight` replaced by `fmt.Errorf("store: preflight: %w", err)` (the code before the fix): **killed** by all four cases of `TestOpenConnectFailuresNeverEchoTheURL`, `TestOpenGivesUpOnAHostThatDropsPackets` and both cases of `TestMigrateNeverLogsAPartOfTheDatabaseURL`.
- **M7** `crossTenantTx.Begin` returns the bare savepoint: **killed** by the savepoint assertion.
- **M8** default connect timeout removed: **killed** by `TestPoolConfigSetsAConnectTimeout`.
- **M9** `Bind` no longer refuses a marked transaction: **killed** by the `tenancy` unit test (nil transaction, panics) and by `TestAHelperRoleTransactionIsCrossTenantWhateverIsBound`.
- **M10** `begin` hand-rolled without the deferred rollback: **killed** by the panic test in 21 s, no hang (`closeWithin` and the 10 s deadline of `assertCleanConnection` do their job). The two cancellation tests stay green, as the implementer said. That is acceptable: nothing in this repository can break what they pin, because it is pgxpool that destroys a connection released in the middle of a transaction, and the comment above the three tests does say the property rests on pgx internals and exists to catch a pgx upgrade. Note only: the comment could say in so many words that the cancellation tests cannot be failed from this package.

### Probes (one throwaway test file, deleted; no scratch containers left)

For each, the error was walked through `Unwrap() error` and `Unwrap() []error`, and every node printed with `%v`, `%+v` and `%#v`, then searched for the user, the password, the host or address, the port and the database name.

`Open` (the unresolvable host, the closed port, the wrong password and the missing database are driven by the new tests, which I ran and mutated, so my own cases are the ones they do not have): wrong password with `sslmode=prefer` (28P01 wins over the joined TLS error); a role without CONNECT on the database (42501, "the role may not connect"); `sslmode=require` against a server without TLS ("TLS negotiation failed"); a listener that answers with an HTTP response ("the connection failed"); a listener that accepts and closes ("connection reset by peer", an errno); a listener that accepts and never answers, with `connect_timeout=1` (timed out after 1.00 s) and with `connect_timeout=0` (timed out after 10.00 s); a context cancelled before the call (`errors.Is(err, context.Canceled)` holds). **No marker in any of them.**

Later failures, through a TCP proxy of my own in front of the test container, so the URL's port was a marker and the proxy could be cut: a statement timeout inside `Tx` (57014, the server's message kept, `errors.As` to `*pgconn.PgError` works); `pg_terminate_backend` from an admin connection while `RoleTx` was inside `pg_sleep` (57P01, message kept, it names nothing from the URL); the proxy cut while `TenantTx` was inside `pg_sleep` ("conn closed"); then, with nothing listening, `Tx`, `TenantTx`, `RoleTx` and `Migrate` each meeting the refused connect lazily ("SLUICEWAY_DATABASE_URL: cannot use the database: connection refused", and `errors.Is(err, syscall.ECONNREFUSED)` holds). **No marker in any of them.**

What callers match on survives `Tx` and `TenantTx` untouched: `pgx.ErrNoRows`; 42501 from the policy with the server's message; 23505 with "duplicate key value violates unique constraint"; 23514 is what the existing domain tests match through `Tx`. So the later branches that match 42501 and 23514 keep working, and the code does tell a connection failure (SQLSTATE only) from a statement that ran (message kept): the first is decided by the error type (`ConnectError`, `OpError`, `DNSError`), not by the presence of a `PgError`.

The wrapper: it satisfies the sqlc `DBTX` shape including `CopyFrom` and `SendBatch` (compile-time assertion, and a batch run inside `RoleTx`); `pgx.CollectRows` works; a savepoint opened through `pgx.BeginFunc(ctx, tx, ...)` is refused; a savepoint of a savepoint is refused. `tenancy` imports only pgx, `store` imports `tenancy`, so there is no cycle and no pull towards one: the marker interface lives on the side that checks it.

### Notes for the merge forward

- `origin/b04-outbox` still carries the old `RoleTx` doc comment ("Inside fn, tenancy.Bind narrows the transaction"), the `db.Ping` test line and the removed `tenancy` identifiers. None of them is changed on that branch, so the merge takes this branch's version. `b04`'s `Claim` does not bind inside `RoleTx`, so the new refusal breaks nothing there.

author: gablooge
text:
## Review, round 1

**Verdict: changes requested**

1 blocking, 3 should-fix, 2 notes. Reviewed `git diff origin/b03-store-rls...e845b2f` only.

**Against issue #4's Done when**
- Two concurrent claimers never get the same row: proven by `TestConcurrentClaimersNeverShareARow`, and the mutation below confirms it has teeth.
- Version 2 is not claimable while version 1 is in flight: proven for that direction. The reverse direction (an earlier row becoming claimable while a later row of the same key is in flight) is not covered and does happen, see the blocking finding.
- A repeated `delivery_id` inserts nothing: proven by `TestAcceptIsIdempotentPerTenant`, per tenant.

**What I checked and found sound.** I walked the claim under READ COMMITTED with two claimers at each boundary. A head locked by a concurrent claimer is skipped, and the row behind it is not taken, because it was not the head in that statement's snapshot. A head that another claimer claimed and committed between the snapshot and the lock is re-checked on its new version and dropped by the lease condition. A takeover racing the old holder's `MarkDelivered` resolves either way round: whichever commits second re-checks and changes nothing. `LIMIT` sits above the row locking, so skipped rows do not shrink the batch. Tenant never comes from a payload, everything goes through `TenantTx` or `RoleTx`, the table forces RLS, and nothing that could hold a secret reaches a log or error string.

**Mutations run (each restored afterwards)**
1. Lease condition removed from the claim: killed, 4 tests fail (`TestSecondVersionIsNotClaimable...`, `TestAnExpiredLease...`, `TestConcurrentClaimersNeverShareARow`, `TestConcurrentWorkersDeliverEachEntityInOrder`).
2. Head-of-key rule removed (every unfinished row is a head): killed, 5 tests fail, including the rewritten concurrent FIFO test.
3. Token guard removed from `MarkDelivered`: killed by `TestAnExpiredLeaseIsTakenOverAndTheOldHolderIsShutOut`.
4. State re-check on the locked row removed (`c.state IN (...)` at queries.sql:28): **survived**, green 3 runs out of 3. See the inline should-fix.
5. Worker `SELECT` grant widened to `raw_body` (and `lease_token` dropped from it): killed by `TestTheWorkerRoleNeverReadsAPayload`. No other test failed, which is how I know the claim does not need to read `lease_token`.
6. `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` dropped on `outbox`: killed, 3 outbox tests plus `store.TestEveryTableForcesRowLevelSecurity`.

**`make check`** on e845b2f: green (tidy, sqlc-check, vet, lint with 0 issues, `go test -race`).

**Note, not in the diff.** `attempts` is only ever consulted by `Fail`. A row whose processing kills or hangs its worker never reaches `Fail`, so it is taken over at lease cadence forever, with `attempts` climbing and no dead letter. Nothing to change in this item, but the worker item should park a row at claim time once `Attempt` exceeds the ladder.

Every finding below was reproduced with a throwaway test against the real migration on testcontainers Postgres, then deleted.
title: Review on PR #32 (commented)

author: gablooge
text:
## Review, round 2

**Verdict: approved**

0 blocking, 1 should-fix, 2 notes. Reviewed `git diff origin/b03-store-rls...1417501`, and `git diff e845b2f 1417501` for what changed since round 1.

**Round 1 findings**
1. **Blocking, two versions of one key in flight: resolved.** I re-ran both of my round 1 reproductions against 1417501. Late commit through the real path: the second `Accept` of the key waits on the advisory lock until the first commits, and claims come out v1, nothing, v2. Late commit with a raw INSERT that bypasses the lock (my original repro): the late v1 is not leased while v2 holds a live lease (the defensive `NOT EXISTS`). Replay while v2 is in flight: the replayed row takes a seq above v2's and is not claimable until v2 finishes.
2. **`clip`: resolved.** Valid UTF-8, no NUL, cut on a rune start, at most 1000 bytes. Mutation (drop `ToValidUTF8`) killed by `TestAnyCauseCanBeRecorded`.
3. **`Replay` forgets `prepared`: resolved.** `prepared_at` is set by `MarkPrepared` and restored by `Replay`. Mutation (`MarkPrepared` no longer sets `prepared_at`) killed by `TestReplayRestoresThePreparedState`. Editing migration 2 in place is fine, it only exists in this pull request.
4. **State re-check unpinned: resolved.** My surviving round 1 mutation M4 (`c.state IN (...)` removed from the locked row) is now killed by `TestClaimRechecksARowFinishedAfterItsSnapshot`. You were right and I was wrong: the window can be hit deterministically.
5. **`lease_token` in the worker SELECT grant: resolved.** Round 1 grant mutation re-run (`raw_body` added to the grant): killed by `TestTheWorkerRoleNeverReadsAPayload`. The remaining grant is exactly the columns the claim reads.

**The correctness argument.** I tried to break it and could not.
- *Lemma.* Both statements that assign a `seq` (`Accept`, `Replay`) take the key's lock first, as a separate statement, and hold it to commit. Nothing else exported assigns one (`acceptIn` is reachable from tests only, through `export_test.go`). The identity sequence has the default CACHE 1, so `nextval` order is real-time order across sessions. Postgres marks a transaction committed in the proc array before it releases its locks, so when y's transaction gets the lock, x is already visible to every later snapshot. Under READ COMMITTED the lock statement and the INSERT have different snapshots, but that does not matter: the lemma is about the claimer's snapshot, and any snapshot that sees y was taken after y committed, which is after x ended. Hence a claimer can never see y of a key without a lower-seq x of that key. `store` opens transactions at the server default isolation level, which is what this relies on.
- *Separator and collisions.* `tenant_id` is a domain over `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$`, so the first `chr(31)` always splits tenant from key even if the ordering key contains one: the lock string is injective. A 64-bit hash collision only serializes two keys. `LockOrderingKey` and `LockOrderingKeyOf` build the same string: changing the separator in one of them is killed by `TestReplayWaitsForAnOpenAcceptOfItsKey`.
- *Uniqueness of the live lease per key.* I re-derived it independently: seqs only grow, so a row whose current seq is below h's had that seq on the claimer's snapshot, was visible there by the lemma, and was finished there; leaving a finished state needs a replay, which moves the row above h. The contradiction for a second live lease r holds on lock times and seq assignment alone, so it also covers a claimer of r that has not committed yet.
- *EvalPlanQual, by experiment.* I built a second, plan-independent pause (a test-only worker SELECT policy whose function blocks the first statement that scans a gate row, which is after the snapshot and before any row lock whatever the plan) and ran both interleavings (finished in the window, died and replayed in the window) under 8 planner configurations (`enable_nestloop`, `enable_hashjoin`, `enable_mergejoin`, `enable_sort`, index scans, seq scans off, in combinations), each on the tiny table and on 36,000 rows after ANALYZE. 32 of 32 correct. With the state re-check removed all 16 state cases fail, with `c.seq = head.seq` removed all 16 seq cases fail. So the stale head row on re-check is real in every plan I could produce (merge join with the seq in the merge condition, hash join, anti join as nested loop, hash and merge), and both re-checks are load-bearing and **not plan dependent**.
- *What EXPLAIN showed (as `sluiceway_worker`).* Default, tiny table: `Update -> Nested Loop (Subquery Scan claimed -> Limit -> LockRows -> Nested Loop Anti Join -> Merge Join on (c.seq, c.id) = (head.seq, head.id)) -> Index Scan outbox_pkey on o`. There is no Sort above the join there, the merge join already yields seq order. On 36,000 rows after ANALYZE: same top, with `LockRows -> Sort -> Nested Loop Anti Join -> Hash Join`. So the reply's "LockRows above Sort and Limit" is not quite it: it is Limit above LockRows, and what makes the locking row by row is the top-level nested loop with `claimed` on the outer side. See the note on `gateClaimOf`.
- *Deadlocks.* `Accept` and `Replay` take one advisory lock and then row locks; the claim and the transitions never take an advisory lock; `LockOrderingKeyOf` reads the row without locking it (and `ordering_key` never changes), so there is no row lock before the advisory lock. A `Replay` racing a `MarkDead` that has not committed sees the row as not dead on its snapshot and returns `ErrNotFound` without waiting. An `Accept` that conflicts on `delivery_id` with an open insert under another key waits for that transaction while holding its own key lock only, and the other side waits for nothing. No cycle.
- *Replay to the back.* `SET seq = DEFAULT` is accepted for the identity column, the row re-enters the partial index with its new seq, `seq` has no unique constraint but only the sequence ever writes it. A replayed `prepared` row delivers records prepared before later versions were delivered; its ledger rows were committed at step 6, so a later version already linked `supersedes` to it, and section 5's forward-only rule covers the late arrival. Section 3.2, the query comment, the `Replay` doc and the migration comment say the same thing.
- *Test-only code.* `test_gate` exists only in `interleaving_test.go` and is created as superuser in the per-test database. Nothing of it is in `migrations/` or non-test code.
- *Randomized stress* (throwaway): 6 acceptors, 8 workers, 4 keys, 30 percent of claims dead-lettered and replayed by a concurrent replayer, in-flight tracked from `Claim` returning to just before the finishing call. 3 runs under `-race`, 240 deliveries and about 100 replays each, never two in flight for a key. The same stress fails under mutation 8 below, so it can see the bug.

**Mutations run on 1417501 (each restored afterwards)**
1. State re-check on the locked row removed (round 1 M4): **killed** by `TestClaimRechecksARowFinishedAfterItsSnapshot`.
2. `c.seq = head.seq` removed: killed by `TestClaimRechecksARowReplayedAfterItsSnapshot`.
3. Worker SELECT grant widened to `raw_body`: killed by `TestTheWorkerRoleNeverReadsAPayload`.
4. `LockOrderingKeyOf` takes no lock: killed by `TestReplayWaitsForAnOpenAcceptOfItsKey`.
5. `LockOrderingKeyOf` hashes with a different separator than `LockOrderingKey`: killed by the same test.
6. `Replay` keeps its seq: killed by 3 tests.
7. `MarkPrepared` does not set `prepared_at`: killed by `TestReplayRestoresThePreparedState`.
8. `Accept` takes the key lock **after** the INSERT instead of before: **survived**, whole package green. See the inline should-fix.
9. `clip` without `ToValidUTF8`: killed by `TestAnyCauseCanBeRecorded`.
10. Defensive `NOT EXISTS` neutralized: killed by `TestAKeyWithAnyLeasedRowIsNotClaimable`.
11. `Replay` without `state = 'dead'`: killed by `TestExhaustedLadderParksTheRowAndReplayRevivesIt`.

**Flakiness.** The interleaving and concurrent tests, `-count=5 -race`: green.

**`make check`** on 1417501: green (tidy, sqlc-check, vet, lint with 0 issues, `go test -race`). CI on the head commit is green.

**Note, not in the diff.** The pull request description still describes the design as first submitted. It says nothing about the per-key advisory lock in `Accept`, replay going to the back of the queue, or `prepared_at`, which are the three things the maintainer most needs to know before merging. Worth updating before it is merged.

author: gablooge
text:
## Review, round 3 (supplementary sweep)

**Verdict: needs maintainer.** 1 blocking (performance), 6 should-fix, 7 notes. Reviewed at dfc5af4. Rounds 1 and 2 stand, and I did not redo the correctness analysis.

The label is `review:needs-maintainer`, not `review:changes-requested`, for the two reasons the rules name: this is a third round with a blocking finding, and the fix is a design decision. Any O(batch) claim changes which conditions sit on the locked row, so the re-check argument of rounds 1 and 2 must be made again, and since nothing polls `Claim` until B10, doing that here or as its own item before B10 is a scheduling call. The finding is not softened by that: as written, the claim does not scale.

| Dimension | What I checked | Findings |
|---|---|---|
| Acceptance | Spot-check (covered in rounds 1 and 2): each "Done when" line of #4 still has its test, all green | 0 |
| Tests have teeth | No code mutations this round (see Probes). Rounds 1 and 2 ran more than 20. Coverage evidence stands in for two mutants, both survive | see next row |
| Tests are comprehensive | Coverage of `internal/outbox` (90.2%), every uncovered block, batch sizes and contexts the tests use, forged `Claimed`, `Ladder` edges, test cleanup | 2 should-fix |
| Correctness | Spot-check: error wrapping in `transition`, `Replay` of a missing row, `LockOrderingKeyOf` is a primary key lookup | 0 |
| Security: isolation, ordering, secrets | Worker grants read back from `information_schema` (SELECT on 8 scheduling columns, UPDATE on 3, `raw_body` refused). `last_error` and `dead_reason` as plain columns | 1 should-fix |
| Security: input, crypto, limits, dependencies | All SQL parameterized. `hashtextextended` input is unambiguous (the `tenant_id` domain excludes 0x1F). Unbounded inputs: `ordering_key` (probed), `raw_body`. No new Go dependency. `govulncheck` not installed | 1 should-fix, 2 notes |
| Performance | `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` as `sluiceway_worker`, real schema, 5,000,000 delivered plus 100,000 and 1,000,000 unfinished rows, 50 tenants, two key shapes, batch 10 and 100, `Accept`, HOT ratio | 1 blocking, 3 notes |
| Dead code | Callers of every exported identifier and generated type, unused columns, indexes, grants | 1 should-fix |
| Codebase improvement | `Row` alias, `State*` constants against the SQL CHECK, error sentinels | 2 notes |
| Documentation | Architecture 3.2, 5, 9, ADR 1, Makefile, README, backlog, godoc, SQL comments, pull request description | 1 should-fix |

Standing rules: attribution trailers, none found. Em dashes in the diff, none found. `make check` on dfc5af4: green.

### Claim measurements

Postgres 17.11, real `roles.sql` and migrations, run as `RoleTx` does and rolled back, 120 byte bodies, analyzed, warm, 5,000,000 delivered rows present (heap 1361 MB).

| Unfinished | Shape | Batch | Returned | Execution | Buffers | How heads are found |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100,000 | 90,000 distinct keys | 10 | 10 | 331 ms | 378,196 | bitmap scan of `outbox_unfinished`, twice |
| 100,000 | same | 100 | 100 | 299 ms | 380,044 | same |
| 1,000,000 | 990,000 distinct keys | 10 | 10 | 4,441 ms | 4,374,969 | **Seq Scan of the whole heap, twice** |
| 1,000,000 | same | 100 | 100 | 4,524 ms | 4,376,997 | same, 5,000,000 rows filtered out twice |
| 1,000,000, all in backoff | same | 10 | **0** | 520 ms | 234,446 | Seq Scan of all 6,000,000 rows |
| 100,000 | 20 hot keys x 4,500, plus 10,000 distinct | 10 | 10 | 584 ms | 273,800 | Seq Scan of the whole heap |

- **O(backlog), not O(batch):** batch 10 and 100 cost the same, about 3 to 4.5 microseconds per unfinished row. Sorts spill 10.6 MB (100k) and 113 MB (1M) per poll.
- **The partial index keeps finished rows out only while the planner picks it.** At 1M, and in the hot-key shape even at 100k, the whole heap is scanned, so retention (B25) becomes a claim-latency concern.
- **An empty poll during a sink outage** costs 520 ms and 1.8 GB of buffer reads.
- **8 drain goroutines at 1 Hz:** 2.4 to 4.7 backend-seconds per second at 100k. At 1M a poll outlasts the interval, 8 backends stay busy, and the default pool of max(4, NumCPU) starves `Accept`. Architecture 9 offers more replicas as more capacity: here they multiply the scans.
- **Threshold (interpolated):** under one core up to about 40,000 unfinished rows, under 10 ms per poll up to about 3,000.
- **O(batch) is achievable:** a SELECT-only probe (candidates in `seq` order, `LIMIT 10`, per-candidate `NOT EXISTS` of a lower unfinished `seq`, throwaway partial index on `seq`) found the same 10 heads on the hot-key table in 0.10 ms and 35 buffers.

Also measured: `Accept` is O(1) at 5,100,000 rows (0.32 ms and 43 buffers for 1 KB, 24 ms for 10 MB). `Get`, `Replay` and the transitions are primary key lookups. All three indexes are used. The claim never reads `raw_body`, so TOASTed bodies do not widen what it scans.

### Notes

1. **HOT updates (B10, B25):** 0 of 10,000 lease and deliver updates were HOT at the default fillfactor. State changes never can be (`state` is in the index predicate). With fillfactor 85 a worst-case probe got 900 of 5,000. Bounded.
2. **No body size cap here (B06):** correct for this layer, but B06 should state a number.
3. **Indexes for later queries (B25, B14):** retention by `finished_at` and listing dead rows have none yet. Rightly so until the queries exist.
4. **`Replay` returns `ErrNotFound` for both "no such row" and "not dead" (B14):** the operator API will want 404 and 409.
5. **`Row` aliases the generated `GetRow` (B10, B14):** the `Get` column list is the public API, and `Row.TenantID` is a `string` where `Claimed.Tenant` is a `tenancy.ID`.
6. **Pool sizing (B10):** `store.Open` leaves pgxpool at its default.
7. **Supply chain and attribution:** the sqlc image is pinned by tag, not digest. The pull request description ends with a tool attribution footer. The standing rule is about trailers, and there are none, so this is for the maintainer to judge.

`State*` constants: each is compared with a stored row by a test, so no finding. Test hygiene is good: one database per test, every wait has a deadline.

### Probes

**No code mutations this round.** Creating a probe test file and editing a tracked file for the first mutant were both refused by the permission system of this session, and I did not work around it. Instead: P1, the `Claim` guard has coverage count 0. P2, tests only pass batches of 10, 7 and 3, so removing the 1000 clamp is invisible to them. P3, the six claim runs above. P4, the O(batch) probe. P5, HOT ratio. P6, `Accept` timing. P7, `ordering_key` against the btree limit. P8, worker grants. The cross-tenant `Claimed` case is reasoned, not run. Both scratch containers are removed, and nothing of mine is left behind.

All findings of rounds 1 and 2 remain fixed as of dfc5af4.

author: gablooge
text:
## Review of the claim redesign (efcf231, 4ca4a74)

**Code verdict: approved.** 0 blocking, 3 should-fix, 5 notes. **Label: `review:needs-maintainer`**, for a reason that has nothing to do with the code: while this review ran, #33 (`chore-agents`) was merged into this branch, so the head moved from 590307d to 15c498c and `git diff --stat origin/b03-store-rls...HEAD -- CLAUDE.md .claude` is no longer empty (3 files, 452 insertions). An agent bound by the rules cannot approve a pull request that carries them. I checked what I can: 15c498c differs from 590307d only in `.claude/agents/*`, `CLAUDE.md` and `.gitignore`, the rules it brings are byte-identical to 95e963a (the rules I was given for this review), its commits carry no trailer, and it contains nothing under `.claude/worktrees/`. All code work below was done on 590307d, whose code is identical to the head.

Two of the three should-fix findings touch liveness and a test that survives a mutation, so by step 5 of the cycle they want one more implementer pass and a delta review. None of them makes the change unsafe to merge on a default Postgres.

### Could I break the new correctness argument?

**Safety (never two rows of one key in flight, never a later seq before an earlier unfinished one): no.** I tried every pair the brief lists, by reading and by experiment. What holds it up is what ADR 10 says: the unique index on heads, the CHECK, and the re-check of `is_head` and `due_at` on the locked row. Specifically:

- The plan keeps `Filter: is_head` on the scan of `outbox_due_heads` although the index predicate implies it (Postgres keeps implied quals on a relation with a row mark, exactly so that the re-check can run them). Seen in every EXPLAIN below.
- `due_at` is STORED, so the re-checked row version carries the value computed by the UPDATE that made it. Proven by two gated probes under all five planner settings: the row is leased by another claimer inside the paused claim's window (paused claim returns nothing, the first holder still delivers), and the row is leased and given a backoff inside the window (nothing, attempts stays 1). Neither case has a deterministic test in the pull request (see note 1).
- Died, everything else of the key finished, replayed onto the empty key inside the window: leased, attempt 1, invariant intact. Died, replayed behind a head that is merely waiting (not in flight): not leased. Both as ADR 10 says.
- Finish then promote are two statements: a claimer sees neither until commit, meets the finisher's row lock and skips, or arrives after the commit and drops the row on the `is_head` re-check. A transaction that fails between the two (I made the promotion raise with a throwaway trigger) rolls back the finish too: the row is still pending, still the head, still leased, and the same lease finishes it afterwards.
- Old holder against new holder after a takeover, finish against claim in both lock orders, Replay against Accept and against a finish, MarkDead against Replay: all serial under the key lock or decided by the token. The unique index check inside the claim's own UPDATE never waits for another transaction, because nobody can insert a second head entry for a key whose committed head is unfinished.
- Deadlocks: advisory before row everywhere, the claim never waits. I found no cycle.

**Liveness (no key stuck without a head): broken once, and only outside the default configuration.** With `default_transaction_isolation = 'repeatable read'` on the database, the package's own `Accept`, waiting for an open `MarkDelivered` of its key, stores version 2 as a non-head after the finish has committed: `0 heads among 1 unfinished rows`, `Claim` returns nothing, no error anywhere. Inline, should-fix. Under READ COMMITTED I could not lose a promotion: context cancellation, an error between the statements and a crash all roll back both statements, and the three lost-promotion tests plus the stress test kill the missing lock.

**The missing state condition: sound.** The CHECK is part of `CREATE TABLE`, so it is validated from birth. A CHECK is not a trigger: `session_replication_role` does not skip it, a superuser cannot write past it, only dropping it removes it, and dropping it fails `TestAFinishedRowIsNeverAHead` and `TestAKeyNeverHasTwoHeads` (mutant C1). The planner claim reproduces in substance: with the condition added back the estimate for the scan falls from 9,520 to 195 rows where there are 10,020 heads, and at batch 1000 the plan leaves the index walk (on my 5.1M row table for a bitmap heap scan of `outbox_one_head` plus a sort, in the guard test for a bitmap AND with `outbox_unfinished`). At batch 10 and 100 my instance kept the walk, so I did not reproduce the 100,202 entry read at batch 100, but the plan is no longer stable, which is the point.

### Round 3 findings

| Finding | Status |
|---|---|
| blocking: the claim is O(backlog) | **fixed**, measured below |
| guard and clamp untested | **fixed**. Mutants F1 (lease guard removed) and F2 (clamp removed) killed |
| errors against `ErrLeaseLost`, cross-tenant `Claimed` | **fixed as far as it goes**: the cross-tenant test is good, the zero value and a copy behave (probe P6). The error test cannot reach the new `finishIn`, see inline (mutant E1 survives) |
| raw error text into `last_error` | **fixed**. No constructor takes text, `WithCode` is 64 bytes of `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]` or the word withheld, mutant F3 killed by the unit test and the database test. The stated limit (a bare token looks like a code) is real and cannot be closed by a character class |
| `ordering_key` bound | **fixed for length** (`len` and `octet_length` are both bytes, 512 and 513 tested, CHECK present). Not for bytes Postgres refuses, see inline |
| unused sqlc structs | **fixed**, `make sqlc-check` green |
| backlog log line | **fixed** |

### Coverage

| Dimension | What I checked | Findings |
|---|---|---|
| Acceptance | the three lines of #4 against their tests, all green at `-count=5 -race` | 0 |
| Tests have teeth | 11 mutants, listed below | 1 should-fix |
| Tests are comprehensive | coverage of `internal/outbox` 94.5% (`finishIn` 75%, the two error returns), the rows of the ADR's window table against the gated tests, stress test detection rates | 1 note |
| Correctness | every pair of operations at every statement boundary under READ COMMITTED, the same under REPEATABLE READ, EPQ on a generated column, rollback between finish and promote | 1 should-fix |
| Security: isolation, ordering, secrets | worker grants read back from `information_schema` and tried by hand, `Claimed` zero value and copy, `Cause` | 0 |
| Security: input, crypto, limits, dependencies | `ordering_key` with NUL and invalid UTF-8, `MaxBatch`, no new dependency, `govulncheck` not installed | 1 should-fix |
| Performance | `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` as `sluiceway_worker` on 6,000,000 and 5,100,000 rows, five shapes, 250,000 lease and finish cycles without vacuum, a held snapshot, a fleet-wide lease expiry, writers on a hot key, a throughput loop before and after | 3 notes |
| Dead code | callers of `acceptIn`, `markDeliveredIn`, every new index, column and grant | 0 |
| Codebase improvement | detection and repair of a broken invariant | 1 note |
| Documentation | ADR 10 statement by statement, architecture 3.2 and 9, roadmap row 10, ADR index, backlog, godoc, the description's table | 0 (the isolation sentence is covered by the should-fix) |

Standing rules: `git log origin/b03-store-rls..HEAD --format='%h %(trailers:only,unfold)'` shows no trailer on any commit, including the seven that arrived with #33. No em dash in the diff. Nothing under `.claude/worktrees/` in the tree. 590307d is a plain merge: `git merge-tree 4ca4a74 2e6699d` conflicts only in `docs/architecture.md`, and the committed tree differs from the automatic one by exactly the six lines of that conflict, steps 1 and 2 of section 3.2 (step 1 from this branch, step 2 from the base). `make check` on 590307d: green. Both outbox packages with `-count=5 -race`: green (33 s and 14 s). CI on 15c498c: pass.

### Measurements

Postgres 17.11, real `roles.sql` (through `sluiceway migrate bootstrap`) and real migrations (through `sluiceway migrate`), autovacuum off, run as `sluiceway_worker` inside a transaction and rolled back, 120 byte bodies, 100 tenants, analyzed, warm. 5,000,000 delivered rows present (heap 1.5 GB, indexes 737 MB). Execution time, shared buffers hit or read.

| Shape | Batch | Mine | The description says |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000,000 unfinished over 990,000 keys | 10 | 0.74 ms, 300 | 0.28 ms, 344 |
| same | 100 | 4.9 ms, 2,466 | 1.1 ms, 3,060 |
| same | 1000 | 29 ms, 24,490 | not given |
| same, every head in backoff, no vacuum, after all 990,000 heads moved in one statement | 10 | first poll 360 ms once, then 7.7 ms, 3,805 | 116 ms once, then 5.9 ms, 3,844 |
| same, after a vacuum | 10 | 0.07 ms, 3 | 0.02 ms, 3 |
| 100,000: 20 hot keys of 4,500 and 10,000 keys of one | 10 | 0.56 ms, 297 | 0.22 ms, 285 |
| same | 100 | 2.1 ms, 2,734 | 1.3 ms, 2,849 |
| same | 1000 | 11.5 ms, 27,417 | 11.6 ms, 28,818 |
| same, the hot heads in backoff | 10 | 0.44 ms, 289 | 0.19 ms, 303 |

Buffers agree within a few percent everywhere, times within the difference between two machines. **O(batch) confirmed**: the search under the Limit node is 4, 7 and 36 buffers for 10, 100 and 1000 rows, the rest is the UPDATE.

What the description did not measure:

- **Churn without vacuum, one row at a time as the application does it.** 200,000 cycles of claim a batch of 100, finish each row, promote, each cycle its own transaction, autovacuum off. A batch of 10 afterwards: 302 buffers and 0.44 ms at the start, 856 after 50,000 cycles, 1,408 after 100,000, 1,960 after 150,000, 2,511 and 3.9 ms after 200,000. Linear, about 11 buffers and 0.018 ms per 1,000 cycles, which is one index page per about 180 dead entries (the ADR says 260: leaf pages are not full). It does not recover on its own, and a VACUUM brings it back to 302 and 0.44 ms at once. See note 2 for what that means under default autovacuum.
- **The same with another session holding a snapshot.** 50,000 cycles while a `SELECT pg_sleep()` ran elsewhere: 50,871 buffers and 10.4 ms per poll, one heap visit per dead entry, as the ADR predicts. After the snapshot is released the next poll costs 7.9 ms once, then 1.4 ms and 839 buffers.
- **A fleet restart.** 10,000 heads leased, every lease ending in the same second. While they are held: 0.27 ms, 57 buffers, nothing returned. After they all expire: 2.7 to 3.5 ms and about 3,050 buffers for a batch of 100. No cliff.
- **Writers on a hot key.** `Accept` of a 1 KB body onto a key with 4,500 unfinished versions: 0.35 ms, 96 buffers. Onto a new key: 0.12 ms, 26. Finishing the head of that key: lock 0.01 ms, state change 0.05 ms and 17 buffers, promotion of the next of 4,499: 0.09 ms and 41 buffers.
- **Write throughput.** 8 acceptors and 8 workers, 4,000 deliveries of 1 KB over 200 keys, accept, claim, deliver, on the test container: 3,300 per second at dfc5af4, 2,630 per second at the head (three runs each, within 3 percent). The marker, the extra index and the two extra statements per finish cost about 20 percent of the write path on an empty table. That is the honest size of "the writers pay for it, a little".
- **Grants**, read back: SELECT on `attempts, due_at, id, is_head, seq, tenant_id`, UPDATE on `attempts, lease_token, lease_until`, no table privilege. Exactly what the claim uses. As the worker: writing `is_head`, `next_attempt_at` or `state` is permission denied, writing `due_at` is refused as a generated column, reading `state`, `ordering_key`, `lease_token` or `raw_body` is permission denied, INSERT and DELETE are permission denied.

### Mutations and probes

| # | Mutant | Result |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | the finishers take no key lock | killed by the three lost-promotion tests every time. The stress test alone: **5 of 10** runs (the description says 4 of 6) |
| S2 | the promotion picks the last row | killed by `TestTheMarkerFollowsTheQueue` and the concurrent FIFO test. The stress test alone: **10 of 10** |
| S3 | `is_head` judged through a self join, so not on the locked row | killed by both gated tests under all five planner settings, and by the guard. The stress test alone: **0 of 10** (note 1) |
| S4 | `due_at` judged through a self join | killed 3 of 3 by `TestConcurrentClaimersNeverShareARow`, the concurrent FIFO test and the stress test. No deterministic test (note 1) |
| G1 | the state condition added back, with the grant it needs | killed by the guard, by the plan's shape at batch 1000 only, as the description says |
| G2 | the claim of dfc5af4, with the grants it needs | killed by the guard in every phase, 16,694 to 20,948 buffers against bounds of 150 to 10,000, the same numbers the description gives |
| C1 | the CHECK `outbox_head_is_unfinished` dropped | killed by `TestAFinishedRowIsNeverAHead` and `TestAKeyNeverHasTwoHeads` |
| C3 | the index on heads not unique | killed by `TestAKeyNeverHasTwoHeads` |
| E1 | a database error inside `finishIn` returned as `ErrLeaseLost` (both error returns) | **survives the whole suite**, inline |
| F1, F2, F3 | lease guard removed, clamp removed, `WithCode` lets text through | each killed |

The stress test logs its seed before anything else, so a failure shows it, takes 1.1 to 1.7 s, and is bounded by a 20 s stall watchdog and a 2 minute context. The guard takes 3 to 4 s, is bounded by a 5 minute context, passed 5 of 5 under `-race`, and cannot be hurt by autovacuum timing: a vacuum only lowers what it measures, and every bound is an upper bound.

Probes (throwaway tests with the pull request's own gate helpers, all deleted): P1 leased inside the window, P2 backoff inside the window (both under five planner settings), P3 replayed onto an empty key and replayed behind a waiting head, P4 a finish whose promotion fails, P5 REPEATABLE READ default, P6 `Claimed` zero value and copy, P7 a finish that times out waiting for the key lock while an Accept of its key is open (an error that wraps the deadline, not `ErrLeaseLost`, and the same lease finishes the row afterwards: the code is right, only the test is missing), P8 keys with NUL and invalid UTF-8. The scratch container is removed and the worktree is clean.

### Notes

1. **Two rows of the ADR's window table have no deterministic test** (leased by another claimer, given a backoff), and they are the two that rest on re-checking a generated column. They are covered statistically (S4 was killed 3 of 3) and my probes P1 and P2 pass, so this is not a gap in the code. The gate helpers make each a twenty line test. The stress test cannot see a missing `is_head` re-check at all (0 of 10), which is fine as long as the gated tests stay, and worth a sentence in its doc comment so nobody leans on it for that.
2. **Default autovacuum is sized by the table, and the claim's housekeeping cost follows it (B25, B10).** The poll cost grows by about 11 buffers per 1,000 lease and finish cycles until a vacuum. Autovacuum fires at 20 percent of the table's rows: at 5,100,000 rows that is about 1,000,000 dead tuples, roughly 500,000 cycles, so about 5,900 buffers and 9 ms per poll just before it fires, against 300 and 0.4 ms just after. Harmless at this size, but it grows with retention: ten times the table is ten times the ceiling. Architecture 9 says "until autovacuum removes them" without saying when that is. A storage parameter on the table (`autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor = 0` with a fixed threshold) makes it independent of how much history is kept. Retention is B25: please copy.
3. **A long snapshot is an ordinary event, not only a bug.** `pg_dump` of a multi-gigabyte outbox, or a stalled logical replication slot, holds the horizon for its whole run. Measured: one page and one heap visit per cycle, 50,871 buffers and 10 ms per poll after 50,000 cycles. At 100 deliveries a second an hour long dump means about 360,000 buffers per poll until it ends. The ADR names the mechanism, the operator documentation (B28) should name `pg_dump` and replication slots.
4. **Nothing at runtime checks the invariant, and the only query for it lives in a test file.** `headsBroken` took 7.7 s on 5,100,000 rows (a full scan, group and sort with 440 MB of temp files), so it is not a monitoring query. A targeted one (unfinished non-heads whose key has no head) reads only the unfinished rows. A stuck key is silent by construction: no error, no log, only a delivery that never happens. A sweep or a metric in B25, with the repair statement written down (take the key's lock, promote the lowest unfinished seq), would turn the chosen failure mode into one an operator can see. Please copy to #25.
5. **Write path, for B10 sizing:** minus 20 percent on the accept, claim, deliver loop (above). The description's per statement numbers are right, the loop number is the one a capacity plan needs.
title: Review on PR #32 (commented)

author: gablooge
text:
## Delta review of 24af3f5

**Code verdict: approved.** 0 blocking, 1 should-fix (a missing doc comment), 5 notes. All three should-fix findings of the previous review are fixed, and I could reproduce every claim in the replies that I tried.

**Label: `review:needs-maintainer`**, for the same reason as last time and not because of the code: `git diff --stat origin/main origin/b04-outbox -- .claude CLAUDE.md` shows 3 files and 452 insertions (they came in with #33). An agent bound by the rules cannot approve a pull request that carries them. The rules I worked from are the ones the orchestrator named (`origin/b04-outbox`, unchanged by 24af3f5: the commit touches no file under `.claude/` and not `CLAUDE.md`).

Reviewed: exactly `git diff 15c498c 24af3f5` (11 files, 946 insertions, 109 deletions), HEAD confirmed at 24af3f5, in an isolated worktree.

### The three should-fix findings

| Finding | Status |
|---|---|
| The design needs READ COMMITTED and nothing asks for it | **fixed.** `store.begin` sends `begin isolation level read committed` (pgx builds it into the BEGIN itself, so no extra round trip). Mutant I1 (`TxOptions{}`) fails all three lost-promotion tests on the REPEATABLE READ and SERIALIZABLE databases and all 16 checks of `TestEveryTransactionIsReadCommittedWhateverTheDefault`, each sub-case in 0.08 to 0.14 s. The reply's claim that all three interleavings strand a row, not only the one I probed, reproduces: `0 heads among 1 unfinished rows` three times under REPEATABLE READ, SQLSTATE 40001 three times under SERIALIZABLE |
| Mutant E1 survives (`finishIn` errors read as `ErrLeaseLost`) | **fixed.** E1 at the lock statement, at the state change, and at the promotion: each killed by exactly its three sub-cases of `TestAFailedFinishIsNotALostLease` (9 of 9), and by nothing else, in about 0.12 s per sub-case. `finishIn` is at 100 percent |
| A key Postgres cannot store is not `ErrBadOrderingKey` | **fixed.** See the experiment below: Go's rule and Postgres's rule are the same rule. Mutants K1 (no NUL check) and K1b (no UTF-8 check) each fail the key test, the provider cases and the id test separately |

Notes acted on: note 1 (a named deterministic test for every row of the window table, and the sentence in the stress test's doc comment), note 4 in its small part (`StrandedKeys` and a written, executed repair), note 5 and the 260 figure (ADR 10 cost section, architecture 9). Notes 2 and 3 are correctly left to B25 and B28.

### The isolation level change, attacked

- **Is `begin` the only place a transaction opens? Yes.** In non-test code the only calls that reach the pool are `pgx.BeginTxFunc` in `begin`, three single statements of the preflight (`pool.QueryRow` twice, `pool.Query` once), and goose through `stdlib.OpenDBFromPool` in `Migrate`. The pool is an unexported field with no accessor, so no other package can open a transaction at all: it is structural, not a convention. `crossTenantTx.Begin` calls `pgx.Tx.Begin`, which in pgx 5.11.0 is `savepoint sp_N` (tx.go:182) and cannot carry a level. `Migrate` runs green with the default set to either other level (the new store test does it).
- **Does anything rely on a higher level? No.** I searched code, SQL and docs for every mention of an isolation level: all of them are the new text. The stress test on a database whose default is REPEATABLE READ passes 3 of 3 at the head, and with the `IsoLevel` reverted it fails in 1.2 s with `could not serialize access due to concurrent update` from the claim. So the claim needed this too, as the ADR now says.
- **What happens elsewhere (facts only, by experiment, no requirement implied).** Role defaults `serializable` AND `default_transaction_read_only = on`: the transaction runs `read committed` and read only, `Open` succeeds, `Get` and `StrandedKeys` work, `Accept` and `Claim` fail with SQLSTATE 25006 (`cannot execute INSERT/UPDATE in a read-only transaction`), wrapped and loud. That is what happened before this commit too. On a real hot standby (I built one with `pg_basebackup -R`): with a default of `serializable`, a plain `BEGIN` fails on its first statement with `cannot use serializable mode in a hot standby`, while the BEGIN that `store` now sends works, reads work, the advisory lock is granted, and a write fails with 25006. So the change makes reads on such a standby possible and changes nothing else.
- **Documented where the next person looks? Yes:** `begin`'s doc comment, the `LockOrderingKey` comment, a paragraph of its own in ADR 10, architecture 3.2, the backlog line, decision 17 of the description. `Tx`, `TenantTx` and `RoleTx` already point to `begin`.

### `storable` against Postgres, by experiment

1,376,512 byte sequences sent to Postgres 17.11 (`convert_from(bytea, 'UTF8')`) and to `utf8.ValidString` plus the NUL check: every 1 and 2 byte sequence, every 3 byte sequence starting E0 to EF, and a grid of 4 byte sequences starting F0 to FF. **0 differ.** The cases that matter, also sent as a text parameter the way the application sends a key: an encoded surrogate half, a CESU-8 surrogate pair, overlong `C0 80`, `E0 80 AF` and `F0 80 80 80`, `F4 90 80 80` (beyond U+10FFFF) and a five byte form are refused by both. U+FFFE, U+FFFF, U+FDD0, U+10FFFF, a leading U+FEFF, DEL and the C1 controls are accepted by both, with the same byte count on both sides (`len` and `octet_length`, so the 512 bound is still bytes on both sides). I found no string that one side takes and the other refuses, on a UTF8 database (note 4 is about the other kind).

### `StrandedKeys`

Finds a stranded key, ignores every healthy shape in the test (queue behind a head, head in flight, head backing off, finished key, dead letter, replayed row), respects its limit and the `MaxBatch` clamp, keeps tenants apart. Mutants K2 (no clamp), K3 (no state condition), K4 (head probe always true), K5 (reverse order) are each killed. The "no false positive on any snapshot" argument is covered by more than the serial test: the stress test runs the stronger `headsBroken` on snapshots of its own during the load.

Cost, on 4,000,000 to 5,000,000 rows (real bootstrap and migrations, as `sluiceway` bound to the tenant, analyzed, warm):

| Tenant | Plan | Time | Buffers |
|---|---|---|---|
| 99,100 unfinished, 90,000 behind 20 heads, rows scattered over the heap as arrivals over time are | merge anti join | 52 to 60 ms | 94,805 |
| the same, nested loops forced (the plan the ADR describes) | one probe per row | 124 ms | 315,245 |
| the same shape, rows physically clustered | merge anti join | 14 ms | 5,709 |
| 100,000 unfinished on ONE key | merge anti join | 12 ms | 4,218 |
| 9,100 unfinished, all heads | | 1.0 ms | 2,083 |
| history only, nothing unfinished | | 0.03 ms | 3 |

So: O(unfinished rows of the tenant), never the history, as documented. The reply's 36 ms and 67,631 buffers sit inside my range. It is about one heap page per unfinished row when the heap is scattered, which is fine for a sweep and would not be for a poll, and the godoc says exactly that. No new index is worth it: an index on unfinished non-heads would be written by every Accept behind a head and every promotion, on the path that already paid 20 percent for the marker, to speed up a query that runs now and then. There is a cheaper win without an index, see the inline note.

**The repair statement** is correct and safe. It takes the key lock first, the ADR says so, and the test runs it as written. What the test does not do is run it against a concurrent writer, so I did (probes P3 and P4): against an open `MarkDelivered` of a healthy key it waits on the same advisory lock as the writers (so the hash expression in the ADR is the right one), then changes nothing, and v2 is delivered. Against an open `Accept` on a stranded key it waits, promotes v1, and v1 then v2 deliver in order. Bound to the tenant as the application role it works too (P5).

### Coverage

| Dimension | What I checked | Findings |
|---|---|---|
| Acceptance | the three lines of #4 are untouched by the delta, their tests green at `-count=3 -race` | 0 |
| Tests have teeth | 14 mutants, listed below, all killed | 0 |
| Tests are comprehensive | coverage of `internal/outbox` 96.5 percent (`finishIn`, `StrandedKeys`, `storable` at 100), every row of the window table against its named test, fail-fast timings, 201 tests run with `-v` and 0 SKIP | 0 |
| Correctness | every way a transaction opens, savepoints, goose, the claim and the stress test under a REPEATABLE READ default, the repair under concurrency at two levels | 1 note |
| Security: isolation, ordering, secrets | `StrandedKeys` runs under `TenantTx` with no new grant and no new role, the worker role is unchanged, the refusal of a bad key still reports only its length | 1 note |
| Security: input, crypto, limits, dependencies | Go against Postgres on 1,376,512 byte sequences, the 512 byte bound, `limit` refused at 0 and below and clamped to `MaxBatch`, no new dependency, `govulncheck` is not installed here | 1 note |
| Performance | `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` of `StrandedKeys` on 4,000,000 to 5,000,000 rows in six shapes, the BEGIN costs no round trip | 1 note |
| Dead code | `StrandedKeys` has no caller outside tests yet, which is deliberate and documented (B25), `errBadProvider`, `storable`, `setupWith`, `get` all have callers | 0 |
| Codebase improvement | the repair exists in the ADR and as a copy in a test constant | 1 note |
| Documentation | ADR 10 (isolation paragraph, window table with test names, cost section, repair section), architecture 3.2 and 9, backlog line, godoc of everything new, the description (decisions 13, 17, 18, the test and mutant lists) | 1 should-fix |

### Mutations and probes

| # | Mutant | Result |
|---|---|---|
| I1 | `begin` without the `IsoLevel` | killed: 6 sub-cases of the three lost-promotion tests, 16 checks of the store test |
| E1a, E1b, E1c | lock error, state change error, promotion error returned as `ErrLeaseLost` | each killed by its 3 sub-cases of `TestAFailedFinishIsNotALostLease`, nothing else |
| S4 | `due_at` judged through a self join | killed by `TestClaimRechecksARowLeasedAfterItsSnapshot` and `TestClaimRechecksARowGivenABackoffAfterItsSnapshot` under all five planner settings (0.14 to 1.4 s each), and NOT by the other four gated tests. The reply's claim reproduces exactly |
| S5 | the claim drops any row whose `seq` changed since its snapshot | killed only by `TestClaimLeasesARowReplayedOntoAnEmptyKeyAfterItsSnapshot`, so the positive row of the table has teeth as well |
| S6 | the claim without `SKIP LOCKED` | killed by `TestClaimSkipsARowSomeoneHasLocked` at its 5 s deadline (6.3 s in all) |
| K1, K1b | `storable` without the NUL check, without the UTF-8 check | each fails the key test, the provider cases and the id test |
| K2 to K5 | `StrandedKeys`: no clamp, no state condition, head probe always true, reverse order | each killed |
| K6 | the provider is not checked | killed by `TestAcceptRefusesBadInput` |

Probes (all throwaway, all deleted): P1 the stress test on a REPEATABLE READ database at the head (3 of 3 green) and with I1 (fails in 1.2 s), P2 serializable and read only defaults through the real `Open`, `Accept`, `Get`, `StrandedKeys`, `Claim`, P3 and P4 the documented repair against an open finish and an open Accept, at READ COMMITTED and at REPEATABLE READ, P5 the repair as the application role, P6 a hot standby, P7 Go against Postgres on UTF-8, P8 a valid UTF-8 key against a LATIN1 database.

### Standing rules

- `git log origin/main..origin/b04-outbox --format='%h %(trailers:only,unfold)'`: 15 commits, no trailer on any of them.
- No em dash and no en dash in the delta, in the commit message of 24af3f5, or in the description.
- Nothing under `.claude/worktrees/` in the tree.
- `git grep -nIP '[\x00-\x08\x0B\x0C\x0E-\x1F]' -- . ':!*.json'` finds nothing. Because `-I` skips any file git takes for binary, and a text file with a NUL in it is exactly that, I also ran `git grep -lP '\x00' -- .` without `-I`: no tracked file holds a NUL byte. The backlog line for B04 is one table row, reads correctly, and its three new sentences match the code.
- `make check` on 24af3f5: green (tidy, sqlc diff, vet, golangci-lint 0 issues, `go test -race`). Run again with `-v`: 201 tests, 201 PASS, 0 SKIP. `internal/outbox`, `internal/outbox/outboxdb` and `internal/store` with `-count=3 -race`: green (37 s, 9 s, 36 s). CI on 24af3f5: pass.

### New findings

**should-fix (inline, `outbox.go`, the `Provider` field of `Delivery`):** refusing an unstorable provider with an unexported error is the right call, but the precondition it rests on (the provider is a constant of the program and never anything taken from a request) is written only on the unexported variable and in the description, not where the author of B06 will read it. It does not touch isolation, secrets, ordering or a surviving mutant, so by step 5 of the cycle it does not need another implementer pass before merge. Please copy to #6.

Notes:

1. **Inline, ADR 10:** the repair snippet says `BEGIN;` and the prose says it must run at READ COMMITTED.
2. **Inline, `queries.sql`:** `AND NOT u.is_head` is implied by the `NOT EXISTS` and costs the heap visit per row.
3. **The repair lives twice** (ADR 10 and the constant `repairKey` in `outbox_test.go`), with nothing tying the two together. They are identical today. If the ADR's statement is edited, the test keeps proving the old one. A comment in the ADR next to the snippet naming the constant would be enough. B25, which will probably turn it into code, can close this for good: please copy to #25.
4. **`storable` is Postgres's rule on a UTF8 database only (B28, or the preflight).** On a database created with another encoding (I tried LATIN1) a perfectly valid key such as `task:` followed by any CJK character or emoji is refused by the server with `character with byte sequence ... has no equivalent in encoding "LATIN1"` (SQLSTATE 22P05), which a caller cannot tell from an outage: the same retry storm the sentinel was widened to prevent, from an ordinary entity id. Nothing checks or documents `server_encoding`. Not this item's to fix. One line in the operator documentation, or one more fail closed check in the preflight, settles it. Please copy to #28.
5. **For B25:** `StrandedKeys` returns ordering keys, which are derived from what a sender sent and may hold any control character except NUL (the key test pins that `\x01\x1f\x7f` is accepted). `Accept` is careful never to quote a key in an error for that reason. The sweep that logs or exports stranded keys should be as careful. Please copy to #25.

author: gablooge
text:
## Review, round 1

**Verdict: approved** (no blocking findings; 12 should-fix, 5 notes). Head reviewed: `f6a6817`.

This pull request has no Go code and no linked issue, so there is no "Done when" list. I reviewed it as what it is: three process documents that must agree with each other, must be executable by a fresh agent, and must not let an agent do what only the maintainer may do. Every `gh` and `git` command in the files was checked against `--help` (gh 2.98.0) or a harmless read-only form, not from memory.

One thing to say plainly: this round was run under the reviewer rules that this pull request itself introduces (the orchestrator pointed me at `origin/chore-agents:.claude/agents/pr-reviewer.md`, as Setup step 7 allows). That is unavoidable for the pull request that creates the rules, and it is also exactly the hole described in the inline comment on `pr-reviewer.md` line 31.

| Dimension | What I checked | Findings |
|---|---|---|
| Acceptance | not applicable: no linked issue, no "Done when" list. Checked the pull request description against the files instead | 1 should-fix (stale description, below), 1 note |
| Tests have teeth | not applicable: no code and no tests in the diff, nothing to mutate. The nearest equivalent is "does each prescribed check detect what it exists to detect", and one does not (the trailer grep) | 1 should-fix |
| Tests are comprehensive | not applicable as coverage. Instead walked Mode 1, Mode 2, a round 1 and a re-review as a fresh agent and looked for the unhandled cases | 2 should-fix, 1 note |
| Correctness | every command: `gh pr view --json` fields, `gh pr view --comments` (does include review bodies, checked on #32), `gh pr create` flags, `gh pr checks --watch`, `gh pr edit --add-label/--remove-label/--body-file`, the replies endpoint, the review-posting call, `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>`, the three `review:*` labels and `backlog` exist, CI triggers on stacked pull requests (`on: pull_request` with no branch filter) | 3 should-fix |
| Security: isolation, ordering, secrets | who can merge, push to `main`, close issues, approve their own work, change the rules they are bound by; whether "read-only" is enforced; no secret or URL in the diff | 4 should-fix |
| Security: input, crypto, limits, dependencies | prompt injection through issue, comment, pull request and file text; running a pull request head's Makefile with the maintainer's credentials. No dependencies added | counted in the row above (same findings) |
| Performance | not applicable: no code path, query or loop in the diff | 0 |
| Dead code | references that point nowhere: step numbers, file paths, labels, `coverage.out` in `.gitignore` | 1 note |
| Codebase improvement | rules written in more than one of the three files, and whether they already differ | 1 note |
| Documentation | `CLAUDE.md` against the repository (paths, `make check` contents, `.claude/agents/`, the `.gitignore` entry is anchored and correct, Go ignores dot-directories so worktrees do not leak into `./...`), the pull request description against the final files, the force-push rule against what commit `5e37f9e` says was done | 1 should-fix, 1 note |

**Standing rules**

- Em dash: none in the diff, none in the five commit messages, none in the pull request body (searched for U+2014, U+2013, U+2015).
- Attribution trailers: none. `git log origin/b04-outbox..origin/chore-agents --format='%h %(trailers:only,unfold)'` prints no trailer for any of the five commits. Note that the check the reviewer file prescribes, `... --format=%B | grep -i co-authored-by`, does NOT print nothing on this branch: it prints two lines, both prose from commit `5e37f9e` ("Rules: no Co-Authored-By trailers, no em dashes"). That is a false positive of the check, not a trailer. See the inline comment on `pr-reviewer.md` line 208.

**Mutations:** none, not applicable (no code). **`make check`:** green on `f6a6817` (tidy, sqlc diff, vet, golangci-lint 0 issues, `go test -race` all packages ok).

**Findings not anchored to a line**

- **should-fix** The pull request description describes the first commit, not the branch. It says the reviewer checks "isolation, exactly-once and ordering, secrets, ordinary bugs, and design drift"; since `f6a6817` every review covers ten table rows and must show a coverage table. It says nothing about the two standing rules becoming blocking (`5e37f9e`), about parallel agents in worktrees and the orchestrator owning the merge-forward (`09a8764`), or about the fact that `5e37f9e` came with a rewrite of the commit messages of every open branch. The implementer file's own Mode 2 step 7 says why this matters: the maintainer merges on the description. It also says "read-only (`Bash, Read, Grep, Glob`)", which reads as if the tool list enforces it; it does not (inline comment on line 4).
- **note** Reviewer Setup step 2 says "Read the linked issue" and gives no fallback when there is none (this pull request). The orchestrator had to supply the acceptance criteria in the prompt. One sentence would do: with no linked issue, the acceptance test is what the orchestrator states, and if it states none, say so in the Acceptance row.
- **note** Reviewer Setup step 6 does not say what to do when an earlier finding cannot be reproduced on re-review. The two bad outcomes are re-raising it unverified (a false finding costs a cycle) or dropping it silently (the thread stays open and looks unresolved). Suggested: say so in the thread and withdraw it explicitly in the status list.

**Questions for the maintainer**

1. `implementer.md` line 50 ends every pull request body with a "Generated with Claude Code" line. You banned attribution trailers in commits and have not said anything about pull request bodies. Keep or drop? (note, inline)
2. `CLAUDE.md` lines 40 to 43 let a fix that touches isolation, secrets or ordering land on an approved pull request with no review, and the `review:approved` label stays. Is that the trade you want? (should-fix, inline)
3. Who reviews a pull request that changes `.claude/agents/` or `CLAUDE.md`? An agent bound by those rules cannot meaningfully approve a change to them. (part of the inline comment on `pr-reviewer.md` line 31)
4. History was rewritten once on the open branches, on purpose. Should that exception be written down, and with what conditions? (should-fix, inline on `implementer.md` line 65)
